author: goytheftauto6
quote:
After 13 years of waiting, GTA 6 is easily the biggest disconnect between critic hype and reality in gaming history. On base PS5, it isn't even a stable 30 FPS—heavy driving and gunfights dip into the teens and low 20s, alongside constant launch bugs.
Worse, Rockstar stripped out the classic GTA sandbox DNA: no mission replay menu, restricted NPC interactions, locked cars, and cut features that made previous games fun. The story also feels heavily one-sided and overly focused on a forced relationship dynamic rather than classic GTA freedom. Lucia is written to dominate every scene while Jason feels reduced to a passive, weak sidekick with awkward, strained voice acting, and the forced Niko Bellic cameo feels completely out of character just for cheap nostalgia points.
Charging $80 for a single-player-only code-in-a-box with no physical disc, pushing GTA+ subscriptions on day one, and likely paywalling GTA 6 Online separately in 2027 is pure corporate greed. Pretty graphics and a big map don't excuse an unoptimized, restricted game that hides behind FOMO and blind hype while locking players out of refunds.
